I don't want to have public APIs that expose people's money and information to easy attack. It's bonkers to me that any financial service would have an API in the first place.

I was a trader for a while. I think the level of communication they're after does exist but it's more through clearing firms(didn't work on that end so I'm not sure). We were absolutely communicating via api with our money accounts.

At the consumer level, this might be more like automating a strategy on ameritrade or other platform. Basically, the ppl who want this functionality can and do get it. It's just not through 'banks'.

A few functions to pull balance and transaction records seems reasonable for a normal consumer but the security investment to offer that might be prohibitive.
